ai.description: *Oligodon brevicauda* (Colubridae) is a small, stout snake reaching 30 cm. It is reddish-brown with a distinct dark nuchal blotch and a notably short, blunt tail. It lacks a loreal scale.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Oligodon brevicauda* is best distinguished by its exceptionally short, blunt tail and a distinct, dark V-shaped marking on the nape that lacks a central light spot.
ai.habitat: The Short-tailed Kukri Snake inhabits the moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Short-tailed Kukri Snake is primarily nocturnal and uses its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice open reptile eggs, allowing it to feed on the contents.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon brevicauda* is oviparous, laying small clutches of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Oligodon brevicauda* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in high-elevation montane forests and grasslands across Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
